# Reference-Aware Synthetic Retention

Add a `reference-aware-synthetic-retention` option, disabled by default, so users can prevent emitted Java from referring to a generated declaration its own output leaves out. When enabled, apply the new decision only to generated declarations that the active removal and reconstruction settings would otherwise omit: synthetic fields, methods, and member classes, and bridge methods. Declare each such member if the emitted Java of its file refers to it, and preserve its omission otherwise. Make that decision from the Java produced by the selected reconstruction settings. Where reconstruction consumes every reference to a generated member, that member remains omitted; where references remain, it is declared under the combination of reconstruction settings that produced them. When the option is disabled, output is unchanged.

A reference is a use of a member by emitted Java code that is itself part of the output. Omitted code refers to nothing, so a generated member reachable only from another omitted member is itself omitted. Text that is not code refers to nothing either, including comments and literal contents. One output file is decided as a whole: a member declared on the outermost class of a file and referred to only from a member class, local class, anonymous class, or lambda body within that same file is referred to.

Retention is decided per member. Declaring one generated member is no reason to declare its unreferenced siblings. Output that needs no generated declarations must not gain any, member for member.

The decision is deterministic for the same input: repeated runs and separate decompiler contexts agree on the same retained members, and a further round, over output that has been compiled again, agrees as well.

## Progress

- Repository: `/app`.
- Added option:
  - `IFernflowerPreferences.REFERENCE_AWARE_SYNTHETIC_RETENTION`
  - ID: `reference-aware-synthetic-retention`
  - short name: `ras`
  - default: disabled (`"0"`).
- Implemented retention in `ClassWriter`:
  - Tracks synthetic fields/methods/member classes and bridge methods.
  - Uses semantic `TextBuffer` tokens, ignoring declarations.
  - Filters references inside comments, strings, chars, and text blocks.
  - Computes a transitive least fixed point across the whole emitted file.
  - Shares state with nested/member/local/anonymous/lambda writers.
  - Avoids rerunning reconstruction processors between passes.
  - Resets annotation write state between trial renders.
- Added constructor-reference tokens in `NewExprent` and `InvocationExprent`, enabled only when the option is active.
- `./gradlew compileJava --no-daemon` succeeds; only existing deprecation warnings remain.

## Manual verification

Temporary JASM fixture `/tmp/TestReferenceRetention.jasm` showed:

- Referenced synthetic method is retained.
- Unreferenced synthetic method remains omitted.
- Synthetic field is retained when emitted code returns it.
- A field access optimized away by reconstruction is omitted.
- Baseline and aware output for `TestClassLambda` were identical.

No repository tests have been added yet.

## Remaining work

1. Inspect and refine the implementation:
   - Add cycle/duplicate protection to candidate collection.
   - Review exact owner/name matching, constructor handling, and method-filter behavior.
   - Check repeated rendering side effects beyond annotations.
2. Run the synthetic switch-map test:
   - Baseline output is in `/tmp/tmp.O6enA5OoeO`.
   - Run the same `TestSwitchOnEnum` case with `--reference-aware-synthetic-retention=1` into `/tmp/tmp.JsrUHsUgiG`, then compare.
3. Add focused automated tests for:
   - default-disabled behavior;
   - per-member retention;
   - reconstruction consuming references;
   - comments/literals not counting;
   - same-file nested/member/lambda references;
   - deterministic repeated runs and recompilation round-trip.
4. Run relevant Gradle tests and review `git diff --check`.

steps.message:
## Current progress

Implemented `reference-aware-synthetic-retention`:

- Preference constant, short name `ras`, default disabled.
- Added whole-file fixed-point retention in `ClassWriter`.
- Tracks synthetic fields/methods, bridge methods, and synthetic member classes.
- Uses emitted `TextBuffer` declaration/reference tokens.
- Ignores comments, string/char literals, and text blocks.
- Includes nested/member/local/anonymous/lambda output in one file.
- Retains enclosing generated member classes when needed.
- Caches reconstruction processing between trial renders and resets annotation write state.
- Added constructor-reference tokens in `InvocationExprent` and `NewExprent`.
- Supports reconstruction-only omissions such as hidden default constructors.
- Added method-selection handling for retained generated fields.

Modified files:

- `src/org/jetbrains/java/decompiler/main/ClassWriter.java`
- `src/org/jetbrains/java/decompiler/main/extern/IFernflowerPreferences.java`
- `src/org/jetbrains/java/decompiler/modules/decompiler/exps/InvocationExprent.java`
- `src/org/jetbrains/java/decompiler/modules/decompiler/exps/NewExprent.java`
- `testData/src/jasm/TestReferenceAwareSyntheticRetention.jasm`
- `test/org/jetbrains/java/decompiler/ReferenceAwareSyntheticRetentionTest.java`

## Verification completed

Manual fixtures verified:

- Per-member retention.
- Reconstruction-consumed field references remain omitted.
- Literal-only names do not retain members.
- Synthetic constructors are retained when `new` still refers to them.
- Synthetic member classes and bridge methods are retained when referenced.
- Switch-map reconstruction produces identical baseline/aware output.
- Existing lambda, annotation, and synthetic-access fixtures remain unchanged.
- Compiled aware output round-trips with the same retained member set.
- Direct `javac` compilation succeeds with only existing deprecation warnings.
- `./gradlew compileJava --no-daemon` succeeded.
- `./gradlew compileTestDataJasm compileTestJava --no-daemon` succeeded.

## Still pending

The targeted Gradle test is currently running:

```text
./gradlew test --tests org.jetbrains.java.decompiler.ReferenceAwareSyntheticRetentionTest --no-daemon
```

Tool session ID: `72952`

Poll it with `write_stdin`. It may take several minutes because `testClasses` rebuilds the test-data graph.

After it completes:

1. Run `git diff --check`.
2. Review `git status --short`.
3. If the targeted test passes, optionally run `OptionParserTest` or the relevant existing tests.
4. Inspect the final diff, especially the method-selection field branch and record-field edge cases.
